The complete fix requires the hemisphere (lat) at the display layer, which is unavailable in any owned file. Root cause: both in-app renderings consume only a pre-formatted weather STRING with no lat. The /weather backend response (backend/routers/weather.py:58-63) returns {formatted, checklist_id, loc_name, obs_dt} — lat is available there (checklist['lat']) but is NOT in the response; WeatherTideSection/WeatherTidePanel and App.tsx's <pre> (state.formatted) both render that lat-less string. A pure emoji->name reverse-lookup is impossible because the mirrored MOON_SOUTH set makes 6 of 8 emoji ambiguous across hemispheres (e.g. 🌒 = North Waxing-Crescent OR South Waning-Crescent); without lat you cannot disambiguate, and announcing the northern name for a southern emoji is the same wrongness the finding reports (no improvement). A display-only span role='img' aria-label fix in WeatherTidePanel's MonoBlock therefore CANNOT announce the correct phase. The genuinely-correct fix is cross-cutting and out of my owned set: add lat (or a moon-phase-name field) to the /weather response (backend/routers/weather.py — not in any accessibility group) and the Tauri parallel (lib/tauri/weatherService.ts — not owned), thread it through the WeatherResponse transport type and App.tsx's <pre> (owned by the app-shell agent), then wrap the header emoji run in <span role='img' aria-label> driven by a new moonPhaseName(unixTs, lat) export. I deliberately did NOT add moonPhaseName to weatherFormatter.ts because with no consumer reachable in scope it would be dead code and would break the byte-parity-trio symmetry (the moon algorithm is duplicated byte-for-byte across weatherFormatter.ts / backend/formatters/weather.py / weatherFormatter.golden.py) without fixing anything. weatherFormatter.ts left unchanged.

The complete fix requires the hemisphere (lat) at the display layer, which is unavailable in any owned file. Root cause: both in-app renderings consume only a pre-formatted weather STRING with no lat. The /weather backend response (backend/routers/weather.py:58-63) returns {formatted, checklist_id, loc_name, obs_dt} — lat is available there (checklist['lat']) but is NOT in the response; WeatherTideSection/WeatherTidePanel and App.tsx's <pre> (state.formatted) both render that lat-less string. A pure emoji->name reverse-lookup is impossible because the mirrored MOON_SOUTH set makes 6 of 8 emoji ambiguous across hemispheres (e.g. 🌒 = North Waxing-Crescent OR South Waning-Crescent); without lat you cannot disambiguate, and announcing the northern name for a southern emoji is the same wrongness the finding reports (no improvement). A display-only span role='img' aria-label fix in WeatherTidePanel's MonoBlock therefore CANNOT announce the correct phase. The genuinely-correct fix is cross-cutting and out of my owned set: add lat (or a moon-phase-name field) to the /weather response (backend/routers/weather.py — not in any accessibility group) and the Tauri parallel (lib/tauri/weatherService.ts — not owned), thread it through the WeatherResponse transport type and App.tsx's <pre> (owned by the app-shell agent), then wrap the header emoji run in <span role='img' aria-label> driven by a new moonPhaseName(unixTs, lat) export. I deliberately did NOT add moonPhaseName to weatherFormatter.ts because with no consumer reachable in scope it would be dead code and would break the byte-parity-trio symmetry (the moon algorithm is duplicated byte-for-byte across weatherFormatter.ts / backend/formatters/weather.py / weatherFormatter.golden.py) without fixing anything. weatherFormatter.ts left unchanged.
